title: Last Orders

opening.text: LP, it's Nadia at the Lobby Bar. I've stopped serving a gentleman, he's had too much. He's wandered into the lobby, he's very unsteady and he says he's lost his room card. Can someone come?

briefing: 00:35. The Lobby Bar has refused service to a guest who has had too much to drink. He is now in the lobby, unsteady, and says he has lost his room key.

Veldane policy: an intoxicated person is first a welfare risk, then a security one. Never leave them alone, never handle them unless their life is in danger, and verify identity before any key or door, however sure you feel.
learningObjectives: Welfare first: assessing an intoxicated person and the medical red flags
Identity before a key, even for an obvious guest
Supporting a refusal of service without confrontation

actions.label: Talk to Nadia at the bar
finding: She served him four large glasses of wine and two whiskies between 21:40 and 00:15, then refused the next and offered water. He took it badly but left.
He tried to charge the bill to room 1409. She did not post it without a key or signature and kept the bill open. He mentioned "pills for my back" while ordering.
rows: Water offered, bill held open: room 1409 not verified

lines.speaker: server_kerr
lines.text: I cut him off at twenty past. He wasn't nasty, just loud. And he said something about pills for his back, which worried me.

actions.label: Speak to the man in the lobby
actions.findingTitle: The man on the lobby sofa
finding: He gives his name as Teodor Halasz, room 1409. Speech slurred, eyes heavy, steady only when seated. He is friendly, embarrassed, and wants "one more for the road".
He took two painkillers for his back at about 22:00. No visible injury. He cannot find his keycard or his wallet; his phone is in his pocket.

lines.speaker: guest_halasz
lines.text: I'm fine. Honestly. One more for the road and I'll go up. Fourteen-oh-nine. My card is... somewhere.

lines.speaker: guest_halasz
lines.text: Took a couple of tablets for my back earlier. It's nothing.

actions.label: Check how he is: breathing, response, injuries
finding: Responds to his name and to questions; knows where he is. Breathing normal. Skin colour normal. No vomiting, no head injury. Cannot walk unaided in a straight line.
Red flags to watch: alcohol mixed with medication, getting harder to wake, vomiting while drowsy, slow or irregular breathing. None present now; reassess every few minutes.

actions.label: Check the registration and ID photo for 1409
actions.finding: Registered to Mr T. Halasz, one guest, three nights. The ID scanned at check-in shows the man on the sofa. One key issued at check-in; none since.

actions.label: Ask the desk to make him a key straight away
actions.finding: Tariq encodes a key for 1409 on your word. It happens to be the right man, but nothing proved it.

actions.label: Have a replacement key made for 1409, old key voided
actions.finding: Identity matched to the registration and ID photo. Tariq encodes one key for 1409; the lost card is voided by the new encoding.

actions.label: Ask Ines to help you take him up
actions.finding: Ines Dalca will meet you at the lifts. Two staff for an unsteady guest: one to guide, one for doors and the lift.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Coming up from B1. Two minutes.

actions.label: Walk him to 1409 with Ines
finding: He walks with Ines at his side and you a step ahead. You open the door with the new key and stay at the threshold. He sits on the bed, agrees to drink water, and you leave the bedside light on.
You do not go further into the room than the doorway. His wallet is on the desk.

actions.label: Arrange a welfare check on 1409 in thirty minutes
actions.finding: You knock and he answers the door, sleepy but clear: "Still alive, thank you." Breathing normal. You log the check.

actions.label: Brief the night manager
actions.finding: Felix Amadi agrees: bill held, a note on the profile for the bar team, and a gentle courtesy call in the morning.

actions.label: Review the bar and lobby cameras
actions.findingTitle: L-07 Lobby Bar and L-04 lobby
actions.finding: The refusal at 00:20 is calm: Nadia offers water, he waves it away and walks out. 00:24 he stumbles on the lobby step but does not fall. No one else is involved.
rows: Refusal; water offered; guest leaves the bar
Stumbles on the step, keeps his feet, sits on the sofa

questions.prompt: He asks you to get him "one more" from the bar. What do you say?

options.label: "The bar's done for tonight, I'm afraid. Let's get you some water and get you up to bed safely. Is there anyone with you tonight?"
options.feedback: You backed the server's refusal without blaming her or him, and turned the conversation to his safety.

reply.speaker: guest_halasz
reply.text: Water. Fine. No, I'm on my own. Trade fair.

options.label: "Just the one, then straight to bed."
options.feedback: Undermining a refusal of service puts the hotel's licence at risk and the guest in more danger.

options.label: "You've had more than enough. Look at the state of you."
options.feedback: True, but shaming an intoxicated person makes them defensive and harder to help.

reply.speaker: guest_halasz
reply.text: Excuse me? I'm a paying guest.

questions.prompt: He mentioned painkillers. Is he a medical case?

options.label: Not now: he is responsive and breathing normally. But alcohol with medication is a red flag, so keep him supervised, check again before and after he goes up, and call an ambulance at once if he gets harder to wake, vomits while drowsy or his breathing changes.
options.feedback: The right balance: no over-reaction, and a clear trigger for calling for help.

reply.speaker: guest_halasz
reply.text: I'm all right. Really. Thank you for asking.

options.label: Call an ambulance now, whatever he says.
options.feedback: Never wrong to call if in doubt, but he is responsive and oriented and has the right to refuse. Supervise and reassess, and call if the red flags appear.

options.label: No. He's just drunk. He'll sleep it off.
options.feedback: "Sleeping it off" is how intoxicated people die alone in hotel rooms, especially with medication on board.

options.label: A registered guest (1409) was refused further service at the Lobby Bar at 00:20, could not find his key, was identity-checked, issued a replacement and escorted to his room by two officers; welfare checks at {time:welfare_check} and {time:welfare_recheck}.
options.feedback: Who, what, when and the welfare actions, without judgement.

options.label: Drunk guest causing trouble in the lobby.
options.feedback: A label and an opinion. He caused no trouble; what did you see and do?

options.label: Guest escorted to room.
options.feedback: True but it leaves out the refusal, the identity check and the welfare checks, which are what protect the hotel.

questions.prompt: Incident report, which of these belong in the findings?

options.label: Service refused at 00:20 after six drinks since 21:40; water offered.
Guest said he took painkillers at about 22:00.
Identity confirmed against the registration and the check-in ID photo before a key was made.
Welfare checks at {time:welfare_check} (responsive, breathing normal) and {time:welfare_recheck} (answered the door).
Guest appears to have a drinking problem.
options.feedback: A diagnosis you are not qualified to make, and it could follow him for years in a file.

options.label: The bar over-served him.
options.feedback: Nadia refused service when she saw the signs. If serving practice is in question, that is for the F&B director, with facts.

questions.prompt: The bar asks whether to post his open bill to 1409.

options.label: Hold it until he can sign it sober in the morning; the night manager agrees.
options.feedback: A charge agreed by someone who could not judge it is a chargeback and a complaint waiting to happen.

options.label: Post it now, he ordered it.
options.feedback: Legally arguable, but you invite a dispute and a complaint. Let him sign it in the morning.

options.label: Waive it as a goodwill gesture.
options.feedback: Above your authority, and it rewards nothing in particular.

checks.label: Welfare before anything else
checks.pass: You checked how he was before you dealt with the key.
checks.fail: The key could wait; his breathing and responsiveness could not.

checks.label: Identity before the key
checks.pass: Registration and ID photo matched before a key was made.
checks.fail: No identity check before a key. Being drunk and sure of a room number is not proof.

checks.label: No key on someone's word
checks.pass: No key was made without checks.
checks.fail: A key was made on your word alone. Tonight it was the right man; the habit will one day open the wrong door.

checks.label: Two staff for the escort
checks.pass: Two officers: one to support him, one for doors. Safer for him and for you.
checks.fail: A lone officer escorting an unsteady guest to his room has no witness and no help.

checks.label: Welfare recheck
checks.pass: You went back to check on him. That is the step that saves lives.
checks.fail: No recheck. Alcohol and painkillers peak after the guest is alone.

checks.label: Hear the server
checks.pass: Nadia told you about the medication, the most important fact of the night.
checks.fail: You never spoke to the server who refused him, and missed the medication.

checks.label: Look at the footage
checks.pass: The cameras show a calm refusal and a stumble, both of which matter if he complains or claims later.
checks.fail: If he says he was injured or mistreated, you have nothing to show what happened.

checks.label: Brief the night manager
checks.pass: The night manager knows, and the bill and courtesy call are in hand.
checks.fail: The night manager learned about it from the bar's complaint in the morning.

debrief.whatHappened: Mr Halasz had six drinks and painkillers on board, and no key. The danger tonight was not a fight, it was a man going to sleep alone with alcohol and medication in him. Checking him, getting him safely to bed with two staff and going back to check is what makes it a non-event.
bestPractice: Talk to the server first: how much, over how long, and anything else taken.
Assess welfare before anything else: response, breathing, injury, ability to walk.
Know the red flags: harder to wake, vomiting while drowsy, slow or irregular breathing, alcohol mixed with medication. Any of them: call an ambulance.
Back the refusal of service without shaming anyone; offer water.
Verify identity against the registration and ID on file before any key, however obvious it seems.
Escort with two staff; stay at the threshold; leave the guest settled with water and a light.
Go back and check, and log every check with the time.
Hold disputed charges until the guest can agree them; brief the night manager.
debrief.why: Intoxication is the most common welfare risk in a hotel at night, and most deaths happen after the person is put to bed and left. Identity checks protect every guest, including drunk ones; two staff protect the guest and the officer from injury and from allegations.
commonMistakes: Treating it as a security problem rather than a welfare one.
Making a key because "it's obviously him".
Escorting alone or going into the room.
No recheck after he is in bed.
Pouring "one more" to keep the peace.

lesson: Welfare first, identity before the key, two to escort, and go back to check.
